title: External Project Evidence And Promotion Inventory

policy.normative_boundary: External project usage is discovery and compatibility evidence only. Engine source, tests, manifests, generated contracts, and Engine-owned examples remain normative.

dispositions.promoted: Reusable behavior has been re-derived from current Engine sources and has an Engine-owned documentation target.
dispositions.boundary-owned: The Engine owns a reusable boundary, while the concrete implementation and policy remain project-owned.
dispositions.promotion-candidate: The observation may be reusable but cannot become normative until its planned artifact, tests, and ownership gate exist.
dispositions.project-owned: The behavior is game-specific and must not be promoted into the Engine contract.

priorities.P0: Required for the standalone production documentation contract.
priorities.P1: Required before the affected public workflow can be claimed production-ready.
priorities.P2: Useful reusable improvement with no current production claim blocked.
priorities.P3: Explicit project boundary; revisit only after reusable code is promoted.

owners.documentation: Information architecture, entry points, maintenance policy, and publication.
owners.build-release: CMake, BuildTools, packaging, updater distribution, and release workflows.
owners.runtime: Applications, client/server runtime, entities, persistence, and lifecycle.
owners.scripting: AngelScript runtime, generated bindings, metadata, and script contracts.
owners.content-data: Configuration, baking, resources, maps, movement, and authored data.
owners.frontend: Rendering, client presentation, and frontend behavior.
owners.networking: Transport, protocol, connection, and synchronization behavior.
owners.tooling: Mapper, editor, and reusable developer tools.
owners.platform: Web, Android, and platform-specific build/debug integration.
owners.quality: Tests, diagnostics, validation, and contributor safety contracts.
owners.localization: Documentation locale parity, terminology, translation review, and language-preserving delivery.

documentation.scope: Information architecture, stable document identity, ownership, maintenance policy, and publication routing.
required_evidence: generated site and AI delivery freshness
co_review_when: a public route is added, replaced, or removed

build-release.scope: CMake, BuildTools, packages, updater distribution, release automation, and reproducible artifacts.
required_evidence: affected build, package, or updater check
co_review_when: credentials, signing, or deployment boundaries are involved

runtime.scope: Applications, entities, lifecycle, persistence, client/server behavior, and runtime compatibility.
required_evidence: migration or compatibility impact where applicable

scripting.scope: AngelScript runtime, metadata, generated bindings, callbacks, properties, events, and script contracts.

content-data.scope: Configuration, baking, authored formats, resources, maps, movement data, and content validation.

frontend.scope: Rendering, GUI runtime, media presentation, visual resources, input, and client-visible behavior.
required_evidence: visible or audible acceptance on every claimed profile

networking.scope: Transport, protocol, connection state, authority, synchronization, and compatibility boundaries.

tooling.scope: Mapper, editors, viewers, helper command lines, generated tools, and reusable authoring ergonomics.
required_evidence: input, output, persistence, and failure contract

platform.scope: Web, Android, host/target toolchains, platform packaging, device behavior, and backend qualification.
required_evidence: device or browser evidence for runtime claims

quality.scope: Tests, diagnostics, analyzers, validation policy, reproducibility, and evidence quality.
required_evidence: clear pass, failure, and residual-risk signals
co_review_when: a gate is weakened or removed
manual evidence is used for a production claim

localization.scope: English/Russian documentation parity, terminology, source freshness, code integrity, and language-preserving delivery.
required_evidence: native-language review and locale link/search checks

records.title: Project bootstrap, staged build, and first launch
records.reusable_claim: A game consumes an exact Engine revision through staged configure, bake, build, and launch milestones with generated outputs kept non-authoritative.
records.promotion_gate: Engine-owned starter and tutorials pass their declared clean-host lanes.
records.decision: Current Engine guides and examples own the reusable workflow; project presets, binaries, ports, and subconfigs stay external.

records.title: Engine submodule update reconciliation
records.reusable_claim: An Engine pin change requires a complete incoming-range audit, generated contract comparison, project integration review, and retained safety state until validation completes.
records.promotion_gate: The Engine procedure remains executable without either project checkout.
records.decision: The Engine owns reusable reconciliation; each game owns its integration consequences and evidence.

records.title: Generated content ownership and dependency order
records.reusable_claim: Source metadata, authored resources, generators, baking, and runtime outputs form an ordered ownership graph; generated output is repaired at its source.
records.promotion_gate: Every generated artifact names its source, generator, validation order, and stale-output signal.
records.decision: Reusable ordering is Engine-owned; project generators and concrete outputs retain project ownership.

records.title: Script modules, lifecycle, authority, and concurrency
records.reusable_claim: Module initialization, callback side, entity covers, async/yield invalidation, events, properties, and generated bindings need explicit ownership and validation.
records.promotion_gate: Claims are tied to Engine callback/export source and focused lifecycle or synchronization tests.
records.decision: Engine lifecycle and binding mechanics are promoted; game module maps, events, remotes, properties, and lock groups remain project-owned.

records.title: Script and native nullability
records.reusable_claim: Nullable script handles and native pointer annotations require one source-backed vocabulary, diagnostics, and analyzer workflow.
records.promotion_gate: Compiler diagnostics and native-boundary checks enforce the reusable contract; declaration-parity and style analyzers remain explicitly project-owned.
records.decision: The Engine guide, compiler diagnostics, and native-boundary checks are normative; TLA migration notes and Last Frontier analyzers remain evidence only.

records.title: Native extensions and project-local dependencies
records.reusable_claim: Role-scoped project C++ sources, optional hooks, generated exports, vendored patches, and platform/package guards need explicit source and compatibility ownership.
records.promotion_gate: The Engine-owned sample compiles and exercises a role-scoped extension at an exact revision.
records.decision: Roles, hooks, and binding rules are Engine-owned; SDK integrations and vendored project libraries stay external.

records.title: Prototype authoring and validation
records.reusable_claim: Prototype discovery, identity, inheritance, property applicability, references, migration, and strict values are parser-owned contracts.
records.promotion_gate: The generated model derives built-in types and properties from current Engine sources.
records.decision: Grammar and built-in properties are Engine-owned; ids, custom metadata, balance, and directory policy stay project-owned.

records.title: Map authoring, baking, and materialization
records.reusable_claim: Map sections, placement identity, ownership, mapper round-trip, side-specific baking, and runtime materialization need one parser-backed contract.
records.promotion_gate: Mapper, baker, loader, and materialization sources agree with generated reference and focused tests.
records.decision: Format and tool mechanics are Engine-owned; map kits, quests, encounters, and level-design policy stay external.

records.title: Text packs, languages, and runtime lookup
records.reusable_claim: Text-pack syntax, duplicate variants, ordered language normalization, prototype text, lookup, and renderer color tags are Engine contracts.
records.promotion_gate: Current parsers, bakers, script methods, and renderer behavior back every format claim.
records.decision: Engine format behavior is promoted; language priority, semantic keys, lexems, pack catalogs, and authored text remain project-owned.

records.title: Models, animation timing, and sprite root motion
records.reusable_claim: Current model grammar, named animation tuples, include templates, tuple AnimSpeed, one-step aliases, exact temporary geometry exceptions, typed durations, 2D frame offsets, movement phase, and stop-time offset normalization must be re-derived from Engine bakers and runtime rather than legacy assets or historical documentation names.
records.promotion_gate: Current parser/baker/runtime sources, focused duration and geometry tests, and visible representative assets replace historical token and implementation-name assumptions.
records.decision: Engine mechanics are promoted. Last Frontier's named-template composition is current project evidence; its 3D *_RM import boundary does not prove 2D offset values. TLA's bare AnimEqual, model-level Speed, raw_ptr, and LoadAnimation names are explicit legacy migration evidence, not current alias, tuple-speed, pointer, or loader contracts. No current authored 2D root-motion asset was observed in either pinned project snapshot, so project offset values and gait-quality claims stay non-normative.

records.title: Effects, images, sprites, and shader resources
records.reusable_claim: Effect state/resources, image inputs, FOFRM composition, baked sprites, factories, atlases, and caches require source-backed format and runtime references.
records.promotion_gate: Baker and runtime models remain current across every claimed renderer/profile.
records.decision: Formats and runtime are Engine-owned; concrete effects, ScriptValue slots, resource precedence, and visual acceptance stay external.

records.title: Particle authoring, baking, tools, and runtime
records.reusable_claim: SPARK and Effekseer are independent optional authoring/runtime paths with explicit baking, bounds, renderer, Mapper, and validation contracts.
records.promotion_gate: Both enabled backends pass source, bake, runtime, tool, and visible integration gates.
records.decision: Engine backend mechanics are promoted; particle catalogs, textures, budgets, and art direction stay project-owned.

records.title: Fonts, audio, and video presentation
records.reusable_claim: Font descriptors/layout, supported audio decoders/playback, and Ogg/Theora video paths require separate Engine contracts and visible or audible project acceptance.
records.promotion_gate: Source and native fixtures back capability claims; each project validates shipped assets on every claimed platform.
records.decision: Engine formats/runtime are promoted; catalogs, typography, mastering, subtitles, licensing, and acceptance stay external.

records.title: Mapper, AnimationViewer, and ParticleViewer
records.reusable_claim: Interactive tool controls, persistence, resource mounting, outputs, recovery, and visible review evidence need Engine-owned manuals.
records.promotion_gate: The stock tools launch against an Engine-owned fixture and changed controls are visibly exercised.
records.decision: Stock tool behavior is Engine-owned; Last Frontier demonstrates project tasks, single-process headless map-preview orchestration, warmup and view plans, developer packaging, assets, and layered acceptance, while the TLA README supplies historical compatibility evidence for a project-owned Mapper target and negative evidence because it has no focused-viewer or reusable capture workflow.

records.title: Client and server profiling
records.reusable_claim: Profiling needs exact tool/version matching, one measured process, reproducible workloads, source zones, export interpretation, and evidence boundaries.
records.promotion_gate: At least one representative Engine-owned capture proves native and script zones with exact tools.
records.decision: Profiling mechanics are Engine-owned; scenes, runners, thresholds, and reports stay project-owned.

records.title: Reusable gameplay and integration test harness
records.reusable_claim: Games benefit from deterministic fixture setup, boundary-based test selection, narrow-first execution, timeout/log contracts, and cross-layer integration evidence.
records.promotion_gate: The project-neutral runner has deterministic positive/failure/timeout coverage, a synthetic fixture, and real baked headless server/client proof in Minimal Multiplayer.
records.decision: Engine now owns boundary-based test selection plus process readiness, marker, deadline, cleanup, and report semantics. Script test registries, game fixtures/assertions, filters, content, persistence backends, platform labs, and acceptance thresholds stay project-owned.

records.title: Native and script safety analyzers
records.reusable_claim: Nullability, smart-pointer, exception-safety, thread-safety, and local-variable policies need Engine-owned contracts and source-backed enforcement boundaries; whole-tree analyzers and baselines remain project-owned until promoted with reusable tests.
records.promotion_gate: Engine documents name exact source/runtime/compiler evidence and distinguish reusable checks from embedding-project analyzers, allowlists, and baselines.
records.decision: Engine contracts and in-repository compiler/runtime checks are normative; whole-tree analyzers, project wrappers, allowlists, and integration baselines stay project-owned until promoted into Engine with tests.

records.title: Project generators, formatters, and content audits
records.reusable_claim: Generated-file discipline and source-level validation are reusable patterns, but concrete project generators and audits are not automatically Engine tools.
records.promotion_gate: Move reusable implementation and tests into Engine before adding any concrete format or command to Engine documentation.
records.decision: Engine documents the ownership pattern; the current GUI/dialog generators, formatters, and audits remain project-owned.

records.title: Dialog tree parser, baker, runtime, editor, and audit
records.reusable_claim: Both games have dialog content, but the current schema, parser, baker, runtime, editor, and audit are not reusable Engine components.
records.promotion_gate: Revisit only after a project-neutral dialog implementation and focused compatibility tests move into Engine.
records.decision: Do not invent an Engine .fodlg contract from project code or authored files.

records.title: Declarative GUI authoring and screen generation
records.reusable_claim: The Engine owns the script GUI runtime, but current declarative file formats, generators, editors, widgets, screens, and styles belong to games.
records.promotion_gate: A declarative format becomes an Engine contract only after its parser/generator, fixtures, and compatibility policy are Engine-owned.
records.decision: Keep runtime mechanics in Engine docs and declarative authoring in each project.

records.title: AI observation and control bridge
records.reusable_claim: Two projects expose AI observation/action bridges, but their schemas, QA commands, MCP adapters, and content semantics are still independently project-owned.
records.promotion_gate: Keep the generated experimental contract, loopback threat boundary, reference client, malformed-peer tests, protocol smoke, and runnable sample current; a native core listener still requires a separate runtime and security promotion.
records.decision: Promote only the transport envelope, authorization, bounded command/event lifecycle, reference client, and protocol sample; keep every project's observation schema, action catalog, administrator tools, and MCP namespace project-owned.

records.title: Cross-platform packaging and release evidence
records.reusable_claim: Package grammar and capability differ from project-qualified host/target release evidence, artifacts, signing, and deployment.
records.promotion_gate: Each claimed host/target package is reproduced from a public minimal project with immutable CI evidence and explicit capability limits.
records.decision: Grammar, current capability, repeatable release procedure, evidence boundaries, and failure routing are documented. The Web guide now separates the build-gated WebGL2 client, stock package/shell/server behavior, WebSocket and browser runtime limits, production hosting, and project browser/release qualification. Last Frontier supplies a required nightly/manual packaged Chromium route with loopback serving, explicit wasm/isolation headers, WebSocket login/token coverage, and a deterministic rendered workload; TLA supplies independent Emscripten presets/settings but no equivalent checked browser-package lane. The Android guide separately covers ARM build gates, source-capable x86, generated Gradle/APK behavior, Wi-Fi ADB, typed server-host launch, debug-key fallback, unsupported native self-update, and project-owned device/store qualification. Last Frontier supplies current ARM64 local workflow and all-ABI nightly build evidence but no official APK artifact; TLA supplies independent settings/presets and ARM build evidence but no device qualification. The Engine packaging fixture and Minimal Multiplayer's own archive/runtime lane are Windows-green, and both native hosts require commit-addressed CI artifacts. The first landed Linux tutorial-package evidence, an exact remotely reachable example pin, immutable external artifact, and owner-authorized publication remain incomplete.

records.title: Updater, secrets, signing, security, and recovery operations
records.reusable_claim: Engine updater and host/runtime mechanics are only one part of production delivery: mature projects keep transfer settings environment-specific, validate installed and portable paths with executable package tests, isolate postfix variants, and sign the exact patched runtime bytes served by packaged servers.
records.promotion_gate: Document only reusable Engine boundaries with redacted fixtures; require packaged-server evidence for native update claims; project credentials, providers, environments, and incident policy stay external.
records.decision: Updater mechanics, installed/portable and variant acceptance lanes, package-time signing of final patched bytes, secret substitution/redaction/handoff, CI isolation, rotation/revocation, incident routing, process/readiness/rollout/shutdown/rollback, and provider-neutral backup/restore/DR boundaries are promoted. Last Frontier supplies broad executable updater evidence; TLA supplies compatibility/configuration evidence but no equivalent updater pipeline lane, so settings alone are not treated as operational proof. Concrete providers, credentials, environments, retention, RPO/RTO, migrations, and production authority remain project-owned.

records.title: Persistence, save migration, and compatibility
records.reusable_claim: Entity persistence, database backends, migration metadata, compatibility versions, backup, rollout, and rollback need separate Engine and project ownership.
records.promotion_gate: Engine storage/migration behavior is source-backed; every game validates its schema/data and recovery path before rollout.
records.decision: Engine mechanics plus provider-neutral backup-set, oplog, restore, and drill boundaries are promoted; concrete schemas, migrations, providers, schedules, retention, objectives, credentials, and production operations remain project-owned.

records.title: Gameplay systems, content catalogs, and balance policy
records.reusable_claim: Quest, combat, economy, AI, faction, survival, and other gameplay systems exercise Engine surfaces but do not define reusable Engine behavior.
records.promotion_gate: Promote only a minimal reusable primitive with Engine-owned source/tests; never generalize a game's rule set into Engine documentation.
records.decision: Keep all gameplay semantics, catalogs, balance, quests, and content acceptance in their game repositories.

records.title: Analytics, live operations, support, and product services
records.reusable_claim: Analytics schemas, support operations, commerce, communications, service providers, and live-ops policy are product concerns rather than Engine contracts.
records.promotion_gate: Only a provider-neutral Engine primitive with source/tests can be promoted; schemas, credentials, KPIs, and procedures remain product-owned.
records.decision: Do not add game operations or service-provider procedures to Engine documentation.

records.title: AngelScript style, refactoring, and change batching
records.reusable_claim: Module ownership, generated-file discipline, narrow change batches, formatter use, and validation-after-refactor recur across projects, but style rules still mix project policy and migration state.
records.promotion_gate: The compact Engine convention is derived from compiler/formatter behavior and Engine CoreScripts, with examples and automated checks independent of project migration plans.
records.decision: Engine owns the enforceable namespace, side/module, formatter, generated-source, mutable-global, attributed-call, batching, and validation baseline. Last Frontier's Test_-only mutable-global/direct-call exceptions and broader project formatter are positive current evidence. TLA's broad production mutable-global allowlist is negative migration evidence, not a reusable default. Project comment language, domain vocabulary, generated formats, migration policy, quality thresholds, and gameplay acceptance remain external.

records.title: Documentation localization and terminology governance
records.reusable_claim: Bilingual documentation needs one canonical locale, stable IDs, mirrored routes, terminology ownership, source hashes, code parity, native review, and language-preserving links.
records.promotion_gate: Locale parity, glossary, hash, code-fence, link, search, and native-speaker review gates are explicit before production publication.
records.decision: The Engine owns its documentation localization process; each game owns player-facing terminology and authored strings.

records.title: Native, mixed-stack, and AngelScript debugging workflows
records.reusable_claim: A production debugging route separates native symbols and debugger semantics, crash-to-log and dump ownership, mixed script/native traces, explicitly enabled loopback AngelScript attach, multi-process selection, live transport capabilities, and focused regression evidence.
records.promotion_gate: Every reusable claim is re-derived from Engine source and native tests; project profiles remain exact pinned evidence, and a static editor profile is never promoted to live endpoint qualification.
records.decision: Last Frontier supplies a strong Windows/Linux native plus AngelScript profile pattern with explicit endpoint enablement, loopback base bind, static validation, and a Linux crash-diagnostic lane. TLA supplies independent compatibility evidence, but its compounds do not explicitly enable the endpoint while its base config disables debugging and uses a wildcard bind; this is negative evidence and not a security or launch template. Engine source and tests remain normative, project target names and incident policy remain external, and the absence of current live endpoint CI is explicit.

records.title: Tutorial assets, provenance, and public examples
records.reusable_claim: Public examples need redistributable minimal assets, exact Engine pins, byte-verified provenance, immutable lesson tags, and pinned/current compatibility evidence.
records.promotion_gate: Every public byte has auditable provenance and each tagged example passes its exact-pin and current-Engine lanes.
records.decision: Governance and clean fixtures are Engine-owned; neither project's game assets are copied into public examples without explicit compatible licensing.
